prompt: The Ottoman Empire after the Young Turk Revolution, 1908
title: The Sublime Porte after the revolution
era: The Ottoman Empire, July 1908 to April 1909
description: Constantinople, 24 July 1908. The Constitution of 1876 is restored today, and elections are called.

sources.title: General Assembly of the Ottoman Empire

grounding: Grounded in the record of the Young Turk Revolution of July 1908, the 1908 Ottoman general election results (275 seats), and the grand viziers' dates of office in the Second Constitutional Era.

fall.what: Said Pasha resigned after the Committee of Union and Progress rejected the Sultan's claim to name the war and navy ministers; Kâmil Pasha replaced him.

factions.name: Committee of Union and Progress
factions.ideology: The secret society of officers and officials that made the revolution. It wants the army ministries and a cabinet it trusts.

face.name: Mehmed Talât Bey
face.role: Member of the Central Committee, Salonika

glance.strike: The Committee brings Third Army officers and Unionist fedai into Constantinople and demands Kâmil Pasha in your place.

factions.name: Liberty Party
factions.ideology: Prince Sabahaddin's liberals, close to the Palace and to Britain. They want decentralisation and officers kept out of government.

face.name: Prince Sabahaddin
face.role: Leader of the League for Private Initiative and Decentralization

glance.strike: The Liberty Party turns its newspapers against the Porte and backs Kâmil Pasha for Grand Vizier.

blocs.name: Muslim peasants of Anatolia
blocs.description: Tithe-paying villagers who fill the regiments, fear the tax farmer and trust the mosque more than the Porte.

blocs.name: Artisans and porters of Constantinople
blocs.description: Guildsmen, boatmen and dock porters who cheered the Constitution and now watch the price of bread.

blocs.name: Muslim townsmen of Rumelia
blocs.description: Shopkeepers, officials and refugees in Macedonia and Thrace who have lived beside the band war for years and want the provinces held.

blocs.name: Greek and Armenian merchants
blocs.description: Traders and professionals of the Christian millets who want equal law but fear losing their church privileges.

blocs.name: Arab townsmen and notables
blocs.description: Merchants, scholars and landed families of Syria, Iraq and the Hejaz who suspect the reformers mean rule by Turks.

patrons.name: Kurdish tribal chiefs of the east

members.name: Mehmed Rauf Karayan
members.bio: From Constantinople, he worked as a gendarmerie clerk in Konya before the 1908 election. He wants Unionist control of the ministries and a paid army.
members.tell: He taps his army pass whenever a deputy mentions the Palace.

glance.strike: He carries the Central Committee's orders to the garrison and blocks the cabinet.

members.name: Hüseyin Cahit Bey
members.bio: From Salonika, he taught Arabic at a Beirut school before entering parliament. He wants a legal cabinet with provincial councils and officers out of politics.
members.tell: He folds each speech into a narrow square and files it by date.

glance.strike: He joins the Liberty Party caucus and demands the cabinet's dismissal.

members.name: Nâzım Efendi
members.bio: From Monastir, he served as a railway inspector and carried dispatches during the Macedonian Struggle. He wants the bands disarmed and the provinces held.
members.tell: He checks the door before every vote.

glance.strike: He summons Unionist volunteers and refuses the ruler's provincial orders.

members.name: Ali Şükrü Bey
members.bio: From Trebizond, he was a customs officer in Erzurum. He wants Armenian land claims rejected and the constitution placed under Islamic law.
members.tell: He rolls prayer beads through every long speech.

glance.strike: He appeals to the Ulema and brings eastern deputies against the ministry.

members.name: İsmail Hakkı Bey
members.bio: From Bursa, he owned a silk workshop and edited a military journal. He wants elected government, but no party to command the army.
members.tell: He sketches cabinet changes in the margins of the order paper.

glance.strike: He publishes the ministry's orders and votes with any bloc against coercion.

members.name: Mustafa Asım Bey
members.bio: From Adrianople, he was a provincial judge before election. He wants regular courts, a disciplined army and a cabinet answerable to parliament.
members.tell: He reads the printed constitution before taking his seat.

glance.strike: He leads a procedural motion to remove ministers who use troops against deputies.

members.name: Ahmed Muhtar Efendi
members.bio: From Damascus, he ran a grain warehouse and entered politics through the city guilds. He wants cheap bread and an army that respects Muslim provinces.
members.tell: He keeps a loaf receipt beside his voting card.

glance.strike: He rallies Arab merchants and withholds his vote on the budget.

members.name: Hasan Fehmi Bey
members.bio: From Constantinople, he was a tobacco broker who settled strikes at the Galata quay. He wants customs revenue spent on wages and bread.
members.tell: He whispers the same price question to every deputy before a division.

glance.strike: He sells his bloc's support to the rival cabinet and calls the debt books corrupt.

members.name: Mehmed Cemal Karayan
members.bio: From Salonika, he was a postal inspector and fedai courier. He wants the Unionist network kept secret and the Palace watched.
members.tell: He burns scraps of paper in the corridor stove.

glance.strike: He sends the Central Committee evidence of betrayal and arranges a private censure.

members.name: Rıza Tevfik Bey
members.bio: From Monastir, he was an Albanian schoolmaster and newspaper poet. He wants a constitution that leaves room for Albanian schools and local rule.
members.tell: He corrects Turkish spelling in other deputies' notes.

glance.strike: He forms an Albanian caucus and votes down taxes imposed without provincial consent.

members.name: Feridun Bey
members.bio: From Smyrna, he worked as a naval pay clerk and later taught French. He wants a secular constitutional state with ministers chosen by parliament.
members.tell: He quotes Montesquieu when the chamber grows loud.

glance.strike: He signs a public demand for a responsible ministry and leaves the chamber.

members.name: Şevket Bey
members.bio: From Baghdad, he was a river customs collector. He wants provincial revenues returned to Iraq and a cabinet able to bargain with Britain.
members.tell: He counts Iraqi revenue figures on his fingertips.

glance.strike: He withholds Baghdad votes and opens talks with the Liberty Party.

members.name: Osman Nuri Bey
members.bio: From Erzurum, he was a cavalry lieutenant and village tax collector. He wants order on the Russian frontier and army pay without foreign supervision.
members.tell: He stands whenever a general enters the gallery.

glance.strike: He asks eastern officers to refuse transfers signed by the ruler.

members.name: Nuri İbrahim Bey
members.bio: From Van, he traded wool and kept accounts for Kurdish landowners. He wants land disputes settled by local councils and the Hamidian police removed.
members.tell: He marks every eastern name on the attendance sheet.

glance.strike: He brings Kurdish chiefs into the capital and breaks the Unionist whip.

members.name: Mehmed Şeref Karayan
members.bio: From Kosovo, he was a railway contractor and armed-road organizer during the Macedonian Struggle. He wants the state to keep its railways and borders.
members.tell: He taps railway times into the desk with a pencil.

glance.strike: He blocks the finance bill and calls provincial officers to defend the railway.

members.name: Halim Sabit Bey
members.bio: From Salonika, he was a law teacher and member of the secret society before 1908. He wants legal reform under a disciplined Unionist cabinet.
members.tell: He underlines each clause before he speaks.

glance.strike: He invokes the constitution and directs the Central Committee to replace the ministry.

members.name: Abdülkadir Kemali Bey
members.bio: From Aleppo, he was a barrister who defended merchants before the military courts. He wants equal courts and provincial budgets under one state.
members.tell: He keeps a folded writ in his breast pocket.

glance.strike: He files charges against ministers and moves his clients into the Liberty caucus.

members.name: Münir Bey
members.bio: From Adrianople, he was a railway guard and reserve sergeant. He wants a strong frontier command and no return to Hamidian censorship.
members.tell: He salutes the chamber clerk before signing attendance.

glance.strike: He uses his railway contacts to bring Rumelian deputies into a no-confidence vote.

members.name: Salih Zeki Bey
members.bio: From Constantinople, he ran a printing press near Babıâli. He wants free newspapers and steady customs receipts for the capital.
members.tell: He smells every new newspaper before reading it.

glance.strike: He prints the ruler's private orders and turns the capital's papers against the cabinet.

members.name: Mehmed Emin Karayan
members.bio: From Konya, he was a village imam and grain buyer. He wants lower taxes, mosque authority and protection for Anatolian recruits.
members.tell: He asks the chamber attendant about grain before every sitting.

glance.strike: He leaves for Konya and calls village notables to resist the ministry's tax orders.

members.name: Kâmil Fevzi Bey
members.bio: From Prizren, he was a medrese tutor and newspaper polemicist. He wants Islamic law protected from Young Turk centralisers and Christian privilege.
members.tell: He closes his notebook whenever a Christian deputy rises.

glance.strike: He joins a petition to the Sultan and urges the chamber to reject equal civic law.

members.name: Yusuf Ziya Bey
members.bio: From Bitlis, he was a tribal secretary who negotiated tax settlements between Kurdish chiefs and officials. He wants local authority and land claims respected.
members.tell: He answers roll call in Kurdish, then repeats it in Ottoman Turkish.

glance.strike: He takes eastern deputies out of the chamber and leaves the ministry without a quorum.

members.name: Hakkı Tarık Bey
members.bio: From Salonika, he was a school inspector and constitutional pamphleteer. He wants elections held on time and ministers named under the constitution.
members.tell: He carries a red pencil for marking breaches of procedure.

glance.strike: He publishes the election timetable and joins the vote to remove the ruler's ministers.

members.name: Naim Bey
members.bio: From Beirut, he was a port lawyer who handled shipping claims. He wants Arab merchants heard in the chamber and equal law for the millets.
members.tell: He translates each Turkish motion into Arabic under his breath.

glance.strike: He builds an Arab caucus and transfers its votes to the rival ministry.

members.name: Süleyman Askerî Bey
members.bio: From Baghdad, he was a staff officer who mapped Ottoman roads and organized supply depots. He wants a modern army and ministers free of Palace control.
members.tell: He measures speeches by the length of a dispatch.

glance.strike: He leaves for Salonika and asks the Central Committee to replace the ruler's cabinet.

members.name: Ahmed İzzet Efendi
members.bio: From Damascus, he drilled recruits in the Second Army before the Constitution. He wants officers to control the ministries and keep the Palace from undoing July.
members.tell: He taps two fingers on the table whenever a palace name is mentioned.

glance.strike: He brings Damascus officers into the capital and backs a Unionist cabinet.

members.name: Mehmed Vedat Karayan
members.bio: From Constantinople, he taught military law at a staff school before entering politics. He wants a single Ottoman army under written constitutional rule.
members.tell: He folds every paper into a narrow military square.

glance.strike: He calls officers to defend the Constitution and blocks Palace orders.

members.name: Arif Hikmet Bey
members.bio: From Scutari, he bought grain for army depots and negotiated with Albanian notables. He wants order in Thrace without breaking the officer network.
members.tell: He counts his prayer beads while weighing each faction's price.

glance.strike: He brokers a military vote against the ruler and recruits provincial allies.

members.name: Şakir Zümre Bey
members.bio: From Salonika, he served as a quartermaster and later ran a tobacco warehouse in Ankara. He wants cheap bread and soldiers paid on time.
members.tell: He tears bread into pieces during every long speech.

glance.strike: He leads Constantinople's guild deputies into a vote of no confidence.

members.name: İbrahim Hakkı Bey
members.bio: From Aleppo, he commanded a gendarmerie district and inspected roads near Mosul. He wants central ministries strong enough to hold the Arab provinces.
members.tell: He marks provincial names in red on a folded railway map.

glance.strike: He gathers Arab deputies behind a Unionist cabinet with tighter provincial control.

members.name: George Karayan
members.bio: From Erzurum, he worked as a railway clerk and carried messages for the Unionist network in Macedonia. He wants equal law enforced by a disciplined state.
members.tell: He corrects Turkish spellings in other deputies' drafts.

glance.strike: He publishes the confiscation lists and breaks with any cabinet that shields officials.

members.name: Krikor Zohrab
members.bio: From Constantinople, he was a barrister who defended Armenian clients under Abdülhamid II. He wants a constitution that protects Armenians from provincial officials.
members.tell: He removes his spectacles before naming a dead client.

glance.strike: He denounces the cabinet in the chamber and joins an Armenian legal campaign.

members.name: Bedros Papazian
members.bio: From Van, he ran a mule train across the Persian frontier before joining the revolutionary network. He wants Armenian villages protected by courts and gendarmes.
members.tell: He keeps a frontier knife on his desk but never touches it.

glance.strike: He withdraws his vote and sends Van petitions to the foreign consuls.

members.name: Sarkis Dadian
members.bio: From Sivas, he owned a printing shop and supplied notices for the Unionist committees. He wants the new law accepted by Muslims and Christians alike.
members.tell: He smells ink on every bill before voting for it.

glance.strike: He uses his presses to expose ministers and organise a constitutional bloc.

members.name: Hagop Deranian
members.bio: From Adana, he taught at an Armenian school and later worked in a cotton office. He wants seized estates returned before local violence resumes.
members.tell: He carries a cotton ledger filled with names of dispossessed families.

glance.strike: He refuses supply votes and calls for an inquiry into Adana officials.

members.name: Vartan Mardikian
members.bio: From Bitlis, he practised medicine among Armenian villages and later joined the Macedonian committees. He wants local self-rule backed by equal courts.
members.tell: He checks the pulse of a nervous colleague before a division.

glance.strike: He crosses the floor and supports a provincial autonomy motion.

members.name: Nikolaos Vlastos
members.bio: From Smyrna, he managed a shipping office and joined the Unionist club after the revolution. He wants customs revenue spent on ports and roads.
members.tell: He checks the harbour timetable while ministers speak about villages.

glance.strike: He withholds commercial votes and calls bankers to oppose the cabinet.

members.name: Dimitrios Sgouros
members.bio: From Constantinople, he was a schoolmaster and municipal clerk before the seat. He wants Christian equality without foreign control of Ottoman courts.
members.tell: He keeps a school attendance book beside the order paper.

glance.strike: He moves an adjournment and joins the Greek and Armenian opposition.

members.name: Emmanouil Pappas
members.bio: From Salonika, he ran a railway office and joined the Unionist central committee. He wants Macedonia held by one law after the Macedonian Struggle.
members.tell: He writes

glance.strike: He recalls railway workers and backs an army ministry against the ruler.

members.name: Yorgo Stavridis
members.bio: From Trebizond, he owned a coastal timber yard and supplied the fleet. He wants Black Sea roads and a government that pays its troops.
members.tell: He carries a splinter of Black Sea pine in his waistcoat pocket.

glance.strike: He joins the naval deputies and refuses the budget until the Palace yields.

members.name: Theodoros Kalogeris
members.bio: From Adrianople, he ran a flour mill before joining a workers' reading room. He wants cheap grain and protection from renewed band war.
members.tell: He asks the price of flour before he asks who made a speech.

glance.strike: He rallies millers and votes down the ministry's revenue bill.

members.name: Ioannis Melas
members.bio: From Chios, he taught navigation and later worked for an Istanbul shipping insurer. He wants merchant law and a navy free from Palace favourites.
members.tell: He draws tiny compass roses beside every amendment.

glance.strike: He brings shipping deputies into a bloc against the Sultan's ministers.

members.name: Moisey Levi
members.bio: From Salonika, he worked as a typesetter for a Jewish newspaper and joined the Unionist press. He wants civic equality and taxes paid by the wealthy.
members.tell: He counts corrections aloud while the chamber waits.

glance.strike: He prints a hostile editorial and votes with the chamber's Christian deputies.

members.name: Isaac Benarroch
members.bio: From Constantinople, he ran a customs brokerage and served on a Jewish communal council. He wants safe trade and an end to arbitrary police searches.
members.tell: He keeps customs receipts tied with blue thread.

glance.strike: He funds a press campaign and backs an inquiry into Palace police.

members.name: Salomon Cordova
members.bio: From Smyrna, he owned a bakery and led a market guild before the seat. He wants bread kept within reach and no return to Hamidian censorship.
members.tell: He gives every visitor a small loaf before discussing votes.

glance.strike: He closes the market guild's shops and joins a public protest against the cabinet.

members.name: Aram Andonian
members.bio: From Constantinople, he worked as a lawyer for railway contractors and joined the Armenian constitutional clubs. He wants contracts enforced and officials checked.
members.tell: He taps a silver pencil against every unsigned contract.

glance.strike: He files charges against ministers and votes to remove the ruler's nominees.

members.name: Mehmed Sırrı Karayan
members.bio: From Kosovo, he ran a postal relay and negotiated with Albanian village chiefs. He wants roads, secure mails and Unionist control of the frontier.
members.tell: He stamps each paper with a private postmark.

glance.strike: He cuts provincial messages to the cabinet and brings Kosovo deputies into opposition.

members.name: Abdullah el-Hadrami
members.bio: From Damascus, he was a court translator and school inspector under Abdülhamid II. He wants Arabic provinces heard without surrendering imperial unity.
members.tell: He translates every Turkish slogan into Arabic under his breath.

glance.strike: He forms an Arab caucus and refuses confidence until provincial councils gain powers.

members.name: Fahri Bey
members.bio: From Mosul, he managed a date estate and served in a cavalry supply office. He wants the army strong and the eastern tribes brought under state law.
members.tell: He rubs dust from Mosul boots onto the chamber carpet.

glance.strike: He backs a security ministry and withdraws support from a weak central cabinet.

members.name: Mehmed Naci Karayan
members.bio: From Scutari, he worked as a civil engineer on waterworks and joined the Unionist club. He wants a legal state that can build and collect taxes.
members.tell: He sketches drains in the margins of every speech.

glance.strike: He blocks appropriations and supports a constitutional ministry without Palace nominees.

members.name: Selim Saffet Bey
members.bio: From Jerusalem, he was an artillery captain in Anatolia before the 1908 rising. He wants the army tied to the Constitution and the Sultan kept from ministerial commands.
members.tell: He taps the table twice when a palace name enters the debate.

glance.strike: He brings his regiment's officers into the Unionist caucus and blocks the palace nominee.

members.name: İzzet Bey
members.bio: From Salonika, he was a railway clerk and reserve officer. He wants cheap bread in Baghdad and a cabinet that answers to deputies, not Yıldız Palace.
members.tell: He stuffs bread prices into every speech, even during army debates.

glance.strike: He calls porters and railway men to a public meeting against the cabinet.

members.name: Midhat Şevket Bey
members.bio: From Monastir, he was a tax clerk who carried messages for Unionist officers. He wants Macedonian order without surrendering the Constitution to soldiers.
members.tell: He leaves the chamber before a vote, then returns with two undecided deputies.

glance.strike: He trades his committee vote for a provincial bargain and quits the Unionist caucus.

members.name: Ahmed Rıza Efendi
members.bio: From Baghdad, he was a schoolmaster and exile in Paris before returning after the Young Turk Revolution. He wants a central Constitution and no return to Abdul Hamid II's rule.
members.tell: He quotes Namık Kemal before opening his papers.

glance.strike: He publishes a signed indictment of the cabinet in the constitutional press.

members.name: Mahmud Nedim Bey
members.bio: From Aleppo, he ran a grain warehouse before becoming a provincial organiser. He wants taxes cut for village markets and army arrears paid on time.
members.tell: He weighs a grain sack on his palm when prices are discussed.

glance.strike: He persuades Anatolian deputies to withhold the budget vote.

members.name: Ali Rıza Bey
members.bio: From Ankara, he was a gendarmerie captain and village mediator. He wants the army ministries under Unionist control and order restored before foreign powers move.
members.tell: He keeps his service revolver belt folded on the chair beside him.

glance.strike: He asks loyal officers to refuse palace orders and protects the Unionist cabinet.

members.name: Mehmed Tevfik Karayan
members.bio: From Erzurum, he was a frontier lawyer who defended Kurdish and Armenian clients. He wants seized Armenian land reviewed by courts and the east kept from another massacre.
members.tell: He writes the names of dead villagers in the margin of every bill.

glance.strike: He denounces the ministry from the floor and sends court papers to Van.

members.name: Hasan Tahsin Bey
members.bio: From Smyrna, he was a customs inspector and provincial judge. He wants ministries run by statute, foreign debt receipts audited, and the chamber recalled on time.
members.tell: He checks the printed agenda against a handwritten rule book.

glance.strike: He leads a procedural censure motion and forces a public division.

members.name: Abdülhalim Bey
members.bio: From the Hejaz, he was a postal superintendent on the Jeddah road. He wants the Arab provinces heard in Constantinople and the caliph's religious authority guarded.
members.tell: He rolls prayer beads under the desk during votes on provincial rule.

glance.strike: He joins the Arab deputies in refusing confidence and appeals to the ulema.

members.name: Kostaki Vayanos
members.bio: From Constantinople, he was a Galata shipping clerk and municipal treasurer. He wants equal law for Ottoman Christians and a solvent state that protects trade.
members.tell: He folds shipping manifests into his parliamentary papers.

glance.strike: He brings Greek merchants into a public delegation against the ministry.

members.name: Leon Arslanian
members.bio: From Adana, he was a cotton broker who organised relief after the 1908 disturbances. He wants courts to return Armenian land and the army kept out of local justice.
members.tell: He removes his fez before naming an Adana village.

glance.strike: He resigns from the caucus and exposes local seizures through Armenian newspapers.

members.name: Rauf Hicazi
members.bio: From Jeddah, he was a customs broker and municipal petition writer. He wants fair grain prices and Arab men admitted to senior provincial offices.
members.tell: He reads every petition aloud before he signs it.

glance.strike: He gathers Hejazi petitions and threatens to block supply votes.

members.name: Şerif Ali Bey
members.bio: From Kosovo, he was a cavalry lieutenant and border tax collector. He wants Albanian schools and a firm Macedonian frontier under constitutional rule.
members.tell: He sharpens a pencil whenever a Bulgarian or Greek band is mentioned.

glance.strike: He carries Kosovo deputies out of the chamber and blocks the frontier budget.

members.name: Maksim Todorov
members.bio: From Adrianople, he was a telegraph operator who joined the 1908 officers' network. He wants reliable wires, a paid army, and no palace censorship.
members.tell: He counts telegraph keys with his thumb during long speeches.

glance.strike: He sends the opposition's statement through provincial telegraph offices.

members.name: Nikola Petrov
members.bio: From Monastir, he was a Bulgarian school inspector and IMRO intermediary before joining the Unionists. He wants equal schools under one Ottoman law.
members.tell: He corrects the spelling of every provincial place name in the minutes.

glance.strike: He votes against the cabinet and calls Bulgarian deputies to a separate conference.

members.name: Stefan Dobrev
members.bio: From Salonika, he was a tobacco merchant and railway contractor. He wants customs reform and a cabinet that can bargain with Austria-Hungary from strength.
members.tell: He compares every promise with the price of tobacco in Salonika.

glance.strike: He takes his commercial bloc away from the budget and demands a new cabinet.

members.name: Lazar Marković
members.bio: From Kosovo, he was a Serbian-language lawyer and district court clerk. He wants local courts protected and the bands disarmed by law, not palace favour.
members.tell: He keeps two legal codes open when provincial powers are debated.

glance.strike: He files a constitutional complaint and forms a Kosovo voting bloc.

members.name: Jovan Ristić
members.bio: From Monastir, he was a railway foreman who sheltered Unionist couriers. He wants wages paid, rail lines guarded, and no return to Hamidian informers.
members.tell: He marks railway towns on the back of the attendance sheet.

glance.strike: He calls railway workers out and gives the Unionist press his evidence.

members.name: Mehmed Şakir Karayan
members.bio: From Thrace, he was a sheep dealer and reserve cavalry sergeant. He wants grain stores opened and the Thracian garrison loyal to the chamber.
members.tell: He smells a coin before accepting it from a petitioner.

glance.strike: He refuses the cabinet whip and brings Thracian deputies into a budget revolt.

members.name: Fatma Hanım
members.bio: From Constantinople, she was a girls' school headmistress and clandestine pamphlet printer. She wants public schools and open newspapers under the Constitution.
members.tell: She underlines each censored word in the official newspaper.

glance.strike: She prints the chamber's censored proceedings and shelters the printers.

members.name: Safiye Hanım
members.bio: From Salonika, she was a telegraph supervisor and Unionist courier. She wants women teachers hired and the army ministries removed from palace control.
members.tell: She taps a code on the desk when Unionist officers enter.

glance.strike: She carries orders to Salonika and cuts the cabinet's telegraph access.

members.name: Elif Hanım
members.bio: From Adrianople, she was a midwife and municipal relief organiser. She wants cheaper bread and courts that protect Christian and Muslim women alike.
members.tell: She carries a household ration book into every sitting.

glance.strike: She leaves the chamber with relief committees and denounces the ruler at the city gates.

citizens.name: Petar Todorov
citizens.worldview: I want the Constitution defended and rival bands kept out of the town.

citizens.name: Katerina Hanım
citizens.worldview: I want equal law and peaceful settlement of contested Armenian land.

starts.premise: The secret society of officers and officials that made the revolution. It wants the army ministries and a cabinet it trusts.
Prince Sabahaddin's liberals, close to the Palace and to Britain. They want decentralisation and officers kept out of government.

problems: The Sultan insists on naming the war and navy ministers himself, and the Committee rejects any cabinet that leaves him those ministries.
The Central Committee in Salonika calls you a creature of the old regime and wants Kâmil Pasha in your office.
Count Aehrenthal in Vienna is preparing to annex Bosnia-Herzegovina, and Prince Ferdinand in Sofia wants to throw off Ottoman suzerainty.
The bands of the Macedonian Struggle have laid down their arms for now, but IMRO and the Greek bands can take them up again.
The Greeks of Crete demand union with Greece, and Athens is waiting for a weak moment at the Porte.
Officers want back pay and a purge of palace favourites, and the capital garrison still takes its orders from Yıldız Palace.
Bread is at famine prices, and the Ottoman Public Debt Administration takes the revenues you would use to lower them.
Armenians in Van and Erzurum remember the Hamidian massacres and want their seized land back, while the Ulema oppose equality for non-Muslims.

deck.memory: He bought one vote and priced every other one.

escalations.name: The press turns
escalations.headline: Tanin and İkdam print your name beside every lost province and every unpaid regiment.

escalations.name: The Committee's Chamber
escalations.headline: Unionists hold 274 of 275 seats, and the Chamber adopts whatever Salonika sends.

escalations.name: Trade stalls
escalations.headline: Harbour trade falls this fortnight, and the customs receipts fall with it.

escalations.name: Hamidian files open
escalations.headline: Old palace files on informers and bribes reach the press, some with your ministers' names in them.

escalations.name: Tempers short
escalations.headline: The Palace and the Committee each give you days, not fortnights, to answer their demands.

escalations.name: A divided Chamber
escalations.headline: Independents and Committee defectors gather against Salonika, and no draft law has a sure majority.

escalations.name: The price rises
escalations.headline: Every deputy and pasha now asks a post, a pardon or a concession for his vote.

escalations.name: Fickle crowds
escalations.headline: The crowds that cheered liberty in July now jeer at the price of a loaf.

escalations.name: Empty treasury
escalations.headline: The treasury cannot meet the officers' back pay this fortnight, and the clerks go unpaid too.

escalations.name: The Palace closes
escalations.headline: Yıldız Palace returns your drafts unsigned and receives your rivals after dark.

escalations.name: Kâmil Pasha rises
escalations.headline: The Committee and the British both speak of Kâmil Pasha for your office.

escalations.name: Empty ballot boxes
escalations.headline: Secondary electors fail to gather in the provinces, and the election canvass stalls.

escalations.name: Ministers waver
escalations.headline: Two of your ministers dine with Committee delegates and stop answering your notes.

escalations.name: Opposition in the squares
escalations.headline: Liberty Party clubs and medrese students fill the squares of the capital against the Committee.

escalations.name: Weary capital
escalations.headline: Each fortnight brings a new crisis, and the Porte clerks no longer hurry to the telegraph.

escalations.name: Leaks from the Porte
escalations.headline: Your cabinet minutes reach Salonika before they reach the Palace.

escalations.name: Mobilisation
escalations.headline: The Army calls up reservists for the Bulgarian frontier, and every spare lira goes to the regiments.

escalations.name: Bread shortage
escalations.headline: Grain runs short in Constantinople, and the bakers raise the price of a loaf again.

escalations.name: The question of the throne
escalations.headline: Talk spreads that the Committee would depose Abdul Hamid II for his half-brother and heir.

escalations.name: The Powers move
escalations.headline: Vienna, Sofia and Athens press on Bosnia-Herzegovina, Bulgarian independence and Crete in the same week.

test.name: Vote of confidence in the Chamber of Deputies
test.win: You keep the Grand Vizierate when a majority of the 275 deputies votes confidence in your cabinet.
test.lose: The Chamber of Deputies votes you down, and the Sultan must name another Grand Vizier.

pork.label: Lira for the vilayet
pork.text: You pledge treasury lira for a road, a school or a barracks in the petitioner's province.

favor.label: A post at the Porte
favor.text: You grant a post, a pardon or a concession now and collect his vote at the next division.

threat.label: The dossier opened
threat.text: You let the petitioner know that his Porte dossier from the Hamidian years could reach the press.

ruler.role: Grand Vizier of the Ottoman Empire, keeper of the imperial seal at the Sublime Porte
ruler.removedBy: Sultan Abdul Hamid II can dismiss you by imperial rescript, the Committee of Union and Progress can force your resignation through the Army and the crowds, and from December 1908 the Chamber of Deputies can bring you down by a vote of no confidence.

persona.name: Georgios Theotokis

briefing.situation: Constantinople, 24 July 1908. The Constitution of 1876 is restored today, and elections are called. Sultan Abdul Hamid II named you Grand Vizier two days ago, after he sacked Mehmed Ferid Pasha. Third Army officers in Salonika made this revolution, and crowds of every millet are cheering them. You want to keep the seal. To do that you must hold the Sultan's trust without angering the Committee, which already has Kâmil Pasha in mind for your office.
briefing.room: Three hands can end your term. The Sultan can dismiss you by rescript from Yıldız Palace. The Committee of Union and Progress can bring out the Third Army and the crowds to force your resignation. From December the Chamber of Deputies can vote you out. The Porte and your ministers are your own machine. The Ulema and the Liberty Party lean your way. The Dashnaks side with the Committee, and the Army is split.
briefing.you: You hold the imperial seal, the Council of Ministers and the clerks of the Porte. You can issue decrees, name governors, spend from a treasury that the Ottoman Public Debt Administration has already raided, and draft laws for the new Chamber. When the Chamber sits, a vote of confidence asks whether a majority of its 275 deputies, 138 votes, backs your cabinet. The election canvass of November and December could give the Committee nearly every seat.
